Drobin New Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Drobin, Poland

Demolished. Likely established in the mid-to-late 19th century north of Drobin's Jewish quarter, this newer cemetery remained in use until the end of WWII, when Germans destroyed it and paved streets with its tombstones. Postwar, part of the site briefly served as an agricultural cooperative warehouse. In 1960, Rabbi Abraham D. Feffer led an effort to recover tombstones from street cobblestones and return them to the cemetery; a matzevah-shaped monument followed in 1964, and the Jewish religious community cleaned and fenced the site in 1975. It's now owned by the Foundation for the Preservation of Jewish Heritage.
